title: cf-review finite quality corpus — ANSWER KEY
warning: This file is the answer key. It must never be inside the scope of a review that is being scored, and its contents must never be pasted into a reviewer prompt. Materialise a case into a git repo OUTSIDE this repository and dispatch the reviewer from there. A review dispatched from a session whose working directory is the coding-friend repo can grep its way to this file; such a run is contaminated and must be reported as contaminated, not scored as a pass.

fixture_policy.synthetic: All fixture code is synthetic. It is never executed, imported, built or linted by this repository; it exists only to be read as a diff.
fixture_policy.no_secrets: No secrets, credentials or user data. Placeholder values use a DUMMY_ marker (DUMMY_APP, DUMMY_EXPORT_BODY).
fixture_policy.no_hints: The fixture trees contain no comment, name or marker that points at a seeded defect. Every hint lives in this file.

scoring.hit_rule: A ground-truth entry counts as a hit when the review reports it in the 🚨 Critical or the ⚠️ Important section (both block a commit; a 💡 Suggestion is a miss), cites the ground-truth file, and its text names the mechanism in must_mention. Reported severity is recorded for transparency but Critical-vs-Important disagreement does not change a hit into a miss.
scoring.false_positive_rule: A false positive is any Critical or Important finding that does not match a ground-truth entry and is contradicted by the code — including any such finding on a bait entry. A blocking finding that turns out to be a real defect nobody seeded is recorded separately as unseeded_true_positive, with the evidence that makes it real. Adjudication is a human judgement and must cite the line it relies on.
scoring.gate_notes: These are the absolute quality gates from the plan README. There is no relative gate against a live baseline: the pre-5.0 specialists took 5–16 minutes each (baseline.md), so a paired live baseline is censored by any run cap worth spending and cannot produce a comparable recall number.

cases.title: Small, genuinely correct change — false-positive control
cases.summary: formatDuration gains a maxParts option that keeps only the N largest units. The implementation, the clamping helper and the new tests are all correct; the required-finding count is zero.

bait.looks_like: An off-by-one: `<=` as the loop comparison.
bait.why_correct: The bound is `UNITS.length - 1`, so `i <= UNITS.length - 1` visits indices 0..length-1 exactly once — identical to `i < UNITS.length`. Verbose, not wrong; at most a 💡.

bait.looks_like: A truncation check in the wrong place — it sits inside `if (value > 0)`, so it is skipped whenever a unit contributes nothing.
bait.why_correct: `parts` only ever grows inside that same branch, so the length cannot reach `maxParts` on an iteration that pushes nothing; checking anywhere else cannot change the output. `normalizeMaxParts` clamps to [1, UNITS.length], so the default still prints every unit and the loop always terminates.

cases.title: Several files with a real correctness bug and a regression-test gap
cases.summary: A cache store is refactored behind an isFresh() helper, a batch runner gains a progress heartbeat and a retry option, and a new report builder is added untracked.

ground_truth.description: The expiry branch in get() is inverted: a fresh entry is deleted and reported as a miss, while an expired entry is returned forever.
ground_truth.must_mention: that the freshness condition in get() is inverted (fresh entries are evicted / stale entries are served) — pointing only at the existence of isFresh, or only at prune(), is not a hit
ground_truth.supporting_evidence: prune() at src/cache-store.js:30 uses the same helper with the opposite sense (`!this.isFresh`), and test/cache-store.test.js asserts the pre-change behaviour.

ground_truth.description: The heartbeat interval is cleared only on the success path, so a task that exhausts its retries leaks a live timer.
ground_truth.must_mention: that clearInterval is skipped when runOne throws (the rethrow at src/batch-runner.js:46 propagates out of runBatch), leaking the interval — the fix being try/finally or an equivalent
ground_truth.supporting_evidence: setInterval at src/batch-runner.js:9; the throw that escapes it at src/batch-runner.js:46.

ground_truth.description: The only test added for the retry feature drives a runTask that never fails, so the retry loop, the backoff and the final rethrow have no coverage.
ground_truth.must_mention: that no test exercises a failing task, so the new retry/backoff/rethrow branch of runBatch is untested — a generic 'add more tests' remark is not a hit

bait.why_correct: `results.length - 1` is the last element by definition and the access is guarded by `results.length > 0` in the same expression.

bait.looks_like: A missing `await`, sitting between awaited calls inside an async loop.
bait.why_correct: CacheStore.set (src/cache-store.js:24) is synchronous and returns undefined; awaiting it would change nothing. The test at test/batch-runner.test.js:45 passes a synchronous stub.

bait.looks_like: An out-of-bounds read on the last row.

cases.title: Larger change with a trust-boundary bug, a missing authorization check and a boundary bug
cases.summary: A document service gains an export route, a delete route, a sorted listing and a pagination helper.

ground_truth.description: Path traversal: the attacker-controlled query parameter `file` is joined onto EXPORT_ROOT and read from disk with no normalization or containment check.
ground_truth.must_mention: that request.query.file is untrusted input reaching the filesystem read (src/document-routes.js:48) and that path.join does not contain `..`, so any readable file can be exported
ground_truth.supporting_evidence: EXPORT_ROOT at src/document-routes.js:7; the read at src/document-routes.js:48.

ground_truth.description: The new DELETE route performs no authorization at all: it never calls assertRole and never calls the canDelete helper added in the same change, so any caller can delete any document, including locked ones and ones they do not own.
ground_truth.must_mention: that deleteDocument has no role/ownership check while every sibling route calls assertRole, and that the change's own canDelete helper is never called
ground_truth.supporting_evidence: assertRole at src/document-routes.js:19, :29 and :43; canDelete defined and exported at src/authorize-request.js:27 with no call site.

ground_truth.description: Boundary bug: slice() is end-exclusive, so every page returns size-1 items and a page size of 1 returns nothing.
ground_truth.must_mention: that the exclusive end should be `first + size`, so the last item of every page is dropped (and size 1 yields an empty page)
ground_truth.supporting_evidence: The slice at src/page-range.js:10; the route that consumes it at src/document-routes.js:32.

ground_truth.anchor: test("exports a document body for a viewer", async () => {
ground_truth.description: The only test added for this change covers the export happy path. There is no test for the new DELETE route and none asserting that a traversal value of `file` is rejected.
ground_truth.must_mention: that the new delete route has no test at all, or that no test covers rejecting a traversal path — a generic 'more tests would help' remark is not a hit
ground_truth.supporting_evidence: Routes registered at src/document-routes.js:13-14; the test file ends at line 70 with no DELETE case.

bait.looks_like: A null dereference — `document` comes straight from a store lookup that can return null.
bait.why_correct: assertExists(document, …) on src/document-routes.js:45 throws NotFoundError when the lookup returned null (src/document-store.js:57-62), so the value is non-null at every later use.

bait.anchor: `SELECT id, title FROM documents WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY ${column} DESC`,
bait.looks_like: SQL injection: a template literal interpolated straight into a query on a request-supplied sort value.
bait.why_correct: `column` is not the user value. The user value is only a key into the hard-coded SORT_COLUMNS map (src/document-store.js:1-5) and an unknown key falls back to `updated_at`, so the interpolated text is one of three literals. The one user-controlled value, ownerId, still goes through a `?` placeholder.

bait.looks_like: A catch block that swallows a job failure after logging it.
bait.why_correct: It rethrows on the same line, so drain() still rejects and the caller still sees the failure; onError is a notification, not a handler.
